object: 200 litre steel oil drum, painted, standing upright outdoors on an oil rig deck
understanding: 1 mm sheet steel rolled into a tube: the wall dents easily and buckles into long creases; the two rolling hoops and the double-seamed chimes at each end are the stiff parts and mostly keep their circle.
Drums get hit side-on (forklifts, other drums, being dropped and rolled), and stacked or run over, which squashes them across the diameter or pushes one end down. They do not fold in half over a bar.

Paint goes first on what sticks out and rubs: the hoops and chime rims. Rust starts where water sits or paint is broken: the recessed lid (a puddle), the bottom chime (standing on wet deck), inside dents and creases, and any scrape.
Rust runs downward from those places as streaks; oil and dirt collect near the bungs and the base.
